title: Scott Colom Wins a Historic Senate Seat in Mississippi
summary:
Mississippi has a new senator, and his win made history.

Democrat Scott Colom beat Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a close race that took days of counting ballots to settle. Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, will become Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since the years right after the Civil War, a time known as Reconstruction. That is a big deal in a state where white conservatives have held power for generations. The last new Democratic senator in Mississippi was picked in 1947, and he supported segregation, the system that kept Black and white people apart by law.

Colom built his campaign around listening. 'They actually deserve a senator that will listen to them,' he said. He said he could represent all of Mississippi, a state where race has long shaped politics and daily life.

Colom's win adds to midterm losses for President Donald Trump's party. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer celebrated the result. Former President Bill Clinton and former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigned for Colom in the closing weeks. Now he heads to Washington as Mississippi's next senator.
why_it_matters: The people who represent your state help make rules that affect your family, your school, and your community.

Reconstruction was the time right after the Civil War when the country worked to rebuild and change its rules.
Segregation was a system of laws that kept Black and white people apart.
Conservatives are people who want to keep things mostly the way they are and change slowly.
